study type: Mixed methods study (quantitative data from randomized controlled trial, qualitative data from interviews)
exposure: Bilingual community-based doula (CBD) support during labor and birth
outcome: Migrant women's experiences of care during labor and birth
Achieving autonomy through communication support and advocacy
Feeling involved during labor and birth
Perception of CBD characteristics (competent, calm, secure, considerate, respectful, encouraging, supportive)
Feeling frightened during labor and birth
cohort: The study participants were migrant women receiving bilingual community-based doula support during labor and birth.
finding: Bilingual community-based doulas significantly contribute to migrant women's emotional, informational, and physical needs during labor and birth, thereby improving their overall experience of care.
